ENDURANCE (LIFE) TEST FOR ELECTRONIC AND ELECTRICAL COMPONENTS
PART II MECHANICAL ENDUJRANCE

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part II) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 6 June 1979, after the draft finalized by the Reliability of Electronic and Electrical Components and Eauioment Sectional Committee and Telecommunication Division had been approved by the Electronics Council.
1 L

0.2 This standard (Part II) deals with mechanical with or without electrical loading as applicable The other mechanical and electrical components. standard covers thermal endurance test.

0.3 This test is primarily intended to be used as part of the type tests, lot acceptance tests or reliability evaluation tests when called for by the relevant component specification which should also give the information as required in 13. 0.4 This electronic published standard is one of a series of Indian Standards and. electrical components and equipment. so far in the series are given on fourth cover. on reliability of Other standards

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard (Part II) describes a uniform test procedure for carrying out mechanical endurance (life) test with or without electrical loading on electronic, electromechanical and electrical components. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this ( Part I)-1977* shall apply.

IS : 9185 ( Part II ) - 1979 3. OBJECT 3.1 The object of this test is to assess the mechanical operational endurance of electronic, electromechanical and electrical components in the normal operating mode with or without a specified electrical loading for a specified number of mechanical actuations/rotations. 4. TEST CHAMBER 4.1 For carrying out this test either required by the relevant specification, in 4.1.1 or 4.1.2 shall be required. at elevated or low temperature, if suitable test chambers as specified

4.1.1 The test chamber shall conform to the relevant provision of IS: 9002 (Part II)-1977* as applicable for carrying out dry heat test in accordance with IS: 9000 (Part III)-1977t both for non-heat dissipating and heat dissipating items. 4.1.2 The test chamber shall conform to the relevant provisions of IS : 9002 ( Part I )-19772 as applicable for carrying out cold test in accordance with IS : 9000 ( Part II )-1977s both for non-heat dissipating and heat dissipating items. 4.2 The test chamber used for this test shall be capable of maintaining the specified temperature within the required tolerance at any point in the working space of the chamber for the required duration. 4.3 The temperature in the chamber shall be checked with temperature sensing devices located so as to comply with the conditions specified in 2.1.2 of IS : 9000 (Part I)-197711. 5. PREPARATION AND MOUNTING OF COMPONENTS

5.1 The components shall be prepared and mounted as required by the relevant component specification in their normal operation position by their normal mounting means. 5.2 With this test conducted at elevated temperature, the relevant precautions as given in 5.2.1 to 5.2.3 for mounting of the components and 5.2.4 shall be observed. 52.1 Care shall prevent excessive components during be taken during the mounting of the components mechanical stress/torque ( for example, bending the mechanical actuations/rotations shall be avoided

IS : 9185( Part II ) - 1979 5.2.2 When groups of components are subjected to tests simultaneously or when mounting racks are used for mounting components, the mounting distances between components and the length of the leads shall be as specified by the relevant component specification. When the distance is not specified, it shall be such as to minimize the temperature of one component affecting the temperature of another. 5.2.3 The thermal conduction and other relevant characteristics of the mounting and connections of the components shall be specified in the relevant component specification. Components intended for use with specific mounting devices shall be mounted accordingly. 5.2.3.1 Where the components are designed for mounting in a heat sink with unspecified characteristics, the heat sink should possess thermal capacity and thermal conduction adequate to maintain its temperature close to the specified test temperature. 5.2.3.2 Where nothing is known about mounting characteristics, the thermal conduction of the mounting shall be low and for all electrical purposes, the components shall be thermally isolated. 5.2.4 Components fabricated of different materials detrimental effect on each other and affect the results be tested simultaneously in the same chamber. 6. SEVERITIES 6.1 The severities, as indicated by the temperature and the number of mechanical actuations/rotations, shall be specified in the relevant specification. PRECONDITIONING 7.1 If necessary, the components relevant component specification. 8. INITIAL MEASUREMENTS may be preconditioned as required by the

8.1 The components shall be visually inspected and electrically and mechanically checked as required by the relevant component specification. 9. CONDETIONING 9.1 Unless otherwise specified, this test shall be conducted atmospheric conditions for testing. at the standard

9.1.1 This test may, however, be conducted either at elevated temperature if so required by the relevant component or at low temperature, specification. In such a case, the relevant component specification shall also state and specify one of the temperature test severities to be chosen from those specified in 6.1.1 or 6.1.2. 9.1.1.1 Thermal conditioning shall be done in accordance with IS : 9000 (Part II s-1977* for conditioning at low temperature and in accordance with IS : 9000 (Part III)-1977t for conditioning at elevated temperature. 9.2 The component shall be exposed to the specified temperature conditions (see 9.1) throughout the test while being subjected to the specified number of mechanical actuations/rotations chosen from the severities specified in 6.1.3. 9.3 Electrical Stresses - When required, the electrical stresses as specified in the relevant component specification shall be applied to the components during this test.
